lab_tasks.instruction: Run bash setup.sh ./work, then open spine-families.txt and crosswalk.csv. State in one sentence each what the spine file is (the set of valid map targets) and what a crosswalk row is (one profile requirement -> spine control + relationship).
lab_tasks.objective: O2 — read 800-53 structure: families as the addressing scheme, family+number as unambiguous control ID
lab_tasks.machine_verify_check: Verify learner viewed both files (sim tracks cat/open events); grade the two definition sentences via keyword/concept match (spine = valid targets / 20 families; row = profile requirement + spine control + relationship label) or short-answer rubric

lab_tasks.instruction: Add three new rows mapping SOC 2 CC7.2 (system monitoring), ISO 27001 A.8.15 (logging), and CIS v8 8.2 (collect audit logs) to spine controls — all three concern logging/monitoring; choose the right family (AU) and an honest relationship label for each.
lab_tasks.objective: O3/O4 — compose honest crosswalk rows; recognize cross-framework convergence onto one spine family
lab_tasks.machine_verify_check: Parse simulated crosswalk.csv: assert 3 new rows exist with profile_control in {CC7.2, A.8.15, 8.2}, each spine_control matching /^AU-\d+/, and relationship in {exact,broader,narrower,partial}; optionally assert CIS 8.2 is labeled narrower (prescriptive safeguard vs broad control) and CC7.2 not labeled exact

lab_tasks.instruction: Find the planted orphan row (PCI4,6.3.2,, — empty spine_control). Do NOT delete it. Decide the correct spine control it should map to (CM-8, system component inventory) and explain in one sentence why mapping it to a loosely-related control would be a false equivalence.
lab_tasks.objective: O5 — diagnose the orphan defect; distinguish honest gap-surfacing from force-fitting
lab_tasks.machine_verify_check: Assert the PCI4 6.3.2 row still exists (not deleted) at this checkpoint; grade the one-sentence explanation via concept match (over-claiming coverage / map claims something the control doesn't do)

lab_tasks.instruction: Run the validator unresolved: bun validate-crosswalk.ts work/crosswalk.csv. Confirm it exits non-zero and names the orphan (PCI4 6.3.2). Capture output into validation-before.txt.
lab_tasks.objective: O5/O6 — machine-readable verdict: validator FAILs on orphan, exit code 1
lab_tasks.machine_verify_check: Sim engine runs deterministic validator logic over current crosswalk state; assert learner executed the command, exit code == 1, and validation-before.txt exists containing 'FAIL: 1 orphan(s)' and 'PCI4 6.3.2'

lab_tasks.instruction: Resolve the orphan by filling in the correct spine_control (CM-8) and a non-orphan relationship label. Re-run the validator and confirm exit 0. Capture output into validation-after.txt.
lab_tasks.objective: O6 — produce a verified, validator-clean crosswalk artifact
lab_tasks.machine_verify_check: Assert crosswalk row PCI4,6.3.2 now has spine_control matching /^CM-\d+/ (canonically CM-8) and relationship in allowed set; validator re-run exits 0; validation-after.txt contains 'PASS: every profile requirement maps to a real spine family'

lab_tasks.instruction: Introduce a deliberate false equivalence: temporarily relabel one of your narrower/partial rows as exact, read it aloud as a coverage claim, state in one sentence why the claim is false, then restore the honest label.
lab_tasks.objective: O5 — experience the false-equivalence defect from the inside; understand the validator cannot catch semantics
lab_tasks.machine_verify_check: Track edit history in sim: assert a row's relationship changed narrower|partial -> exact and then back; grade the one-sentence justification via concept match (control does not fully satisfy the requirement / over-claims coverage)

lab_tasks.instruction: Write a 4-6 sentence README.md for the crosswalk explaining: what the spine is, why 800-53 is the spine and not one of the profiles (superset argument), how to read a row's relationship label, and what the validator guarantees vs deliberately cannot guarantee (semantic honesty is human-supplied).
lab_tasks.objective: O1/O6 — articulate the spine-and-profile model and the machine/human division of labor
lab_tasks.machine_verify_check: Assert README.md exists with 4-6 sentences; rubric/keyword grading for the four required concepts: spine definition, superset rationale, relationship-label reading, validator guarantee boundary

lab_setup_state: setup.sh [DEST_DIR] (default ./work) creates two files, fully offline, no network/cloud/subscription. (1) work/spine-families.txt — exactly 20 lines, the NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control-family abbreviations: AC, AT, AU, CA, CM, CP, IA, IR, MA, MP, PE, PL, PM, PS, PT, RA, SA, SC, SI, SR. These are the only valid map targets; a row's spine_control must begin with one of them. (2) work/crosswalk.csv — header 'profile,profile_control,spine_control,relationship' plus 4 seed rows: 'SOC2,CC6.1,AC-2,broader', 'ISO27001,A.5.15,AC-2,exact', 'CSF2,PR.DS-01,SC-28,partial', and the intentional planted orphan 'PCI4,6.3.2,,orphan' (empty spine_control). The reference validator validate-crosswalk.ts (bun, dependency-free) lives in labs/ and takes <crosswalk.csv> [spine-families.txt] (families path defaults to dirname(csv)/spine-families.txt). Validator logic: header must match exactly; a row is an orphan if spine_control is empty OR relationship=='orphan'; non-orphan rows must have spine_control whose prefix before '-' is in the families set and relationship in {exact,broader,narrower,partial}; prints 'profiles: N | rows: N | spine families referenced: N/20' summary line then FAIL sections or PASS line; exit 0 clean / 1 on any defect. Requires Unix-like shell + bun (or the awk fallback in happy-path.sh). ~60-90 minutes, Tier-B content.
assessment_artifact: Timed (45 min, unaided) competency artifact from a fresh unseen set of 8-12 profile requirements drawn from 3+ frameworks (e.g. SOC 2 CC criteria, ISO 27001 Annex A, CIS v8 safeguards, optionally PCI/HIPAA), including one genuine orphan candidate and one pre-filled sample row deliberately mislabeled 'exact' (the planted false-equivalence trap). Learner delivers: (1) a crosswalk file (CSV or JSON) mapping every requirement to one or more 800-53 spine controls with honest relationship labels, genuinely unmappable requirements recorded explicitly as orphans rather than force-fit; (2) two validator runs — FAIL on the orphan then PASS after resolution or formal acceptance as a documented spine gap, exit code as the verdict in both; (3) a walkthrough that explains why 800-53 is the spine and the others profiles, justifies two rows' relationship labels, and identifies the planted false-equivalence row. Scored against rubric.md: 6 Pass/Not-yet criteria (Spine vs profile/O1->§3, Spine literacy/O2->§4.1, Framework shapes/O3->§4.2-4.5, Honest mapping/O4->§4.6, Defect diagnosis/O5->§4.7, Verified artifact/O6->§4.7-4.8+§6); all must Pass; a Not-yet routes to the named concept section. Pass-rate threshold 0.80.

exercise_design.sim_state: Virtual filesystem seeded exactly as setup.sh produces it: work/spine-families.txt (20 families) and work/crosswalk.csv (header + 4 seed rows incl. the PCI4,6.3.2 planted orphan), plus labs/validate-crosswalk.ts conceptually present. The validator is trivially re-implementable client-side in JS with byte-identical output (pure CSV parsing + set membership + counters) — port the exact TypeScript logic so 'bun validate-crosswalk.ts <path>' in the terminal-sim produces the real summary line, FAIL/PASS sections, and exit codes against whatever the learner's current crosswalk.csv state is. Terminal-sim state: cwd, files (crosswalk.csv mutable via editor pane), command history, $? for exit-code checks, output redirection to validation-before.txt/validation-after.txt.
exercise_design.notes: This module is unusually well suited to a high-fidelity static-web exercise because its entire verification loop (CSV in, deterministic validator out) is dependency-free and portable to client-side JS. Recommended design: a split-pane app — left: editable crosswalk.csv in a CSV-aware editor (or structured row-builder with dropdowns for profile, spine family, control number, relationship); right: terminal-sim that runs the byte-faithful validator port. Tasks: (1) warm-up matching-mapping exercise — drag framework descriptions (attestation report w/ TSC, certifiable ISMS, outcomes-by-function, prescriptive safeguard list) onto SOC 2 / ISO 27001 / CSF 2.0 / CIS v8 to lock in §4.2-4.5 'what kind of object is it'; (2) spine-literacy drill — given AC-2, AU-6, CM-8, IR-4, parse family + number and pick the family name from the 20; (3-8) the seven guided-lab tasks compressed: add the three logging rows (structured-builder with relationship dropdown forces a deliberate honesty call, mirroring the validator's design philosophy), run validator -> see FAIL naming PCI4 6.3.2, capture to validation-before.txt, resolve orphan to CM-8, run -> PASS, capture validation-after.txt; (9) false-equivalence trap — present a pre-filled row labeled 'exact' that is honestly 'partial' (e.g. CSF2,PR.DS-01,SC-28,exact) and require the learner to spot and relabel it, mirroring the assessment's planted trap. Grade structurally where the validator grades (orphans, families, vocabulary) and via concept-keyword rubric where a human grades (the one-sentence honesty justifications) — the module itself teaches exactly this machine/human split, so the exercise engine should embody it. Include the exit-code concept explicitly: show 'exit: 1'/'echo $?' in the sim, since 'exit code as the verdict' is rubric row O6. Avoid free-form mapping of unfamiliar requirements without scaffolding — the lab pre-decides the targets (AU family, CM-8); the assessment is where open mapping happens.

fidelity_notes: All validator outputs above were captured by actually running the shipped scripts on macOS with bun (fidelity high; pure POSIX + bun, no platform variance). One discrepancy to preserve deliberately: module.md §5.4 shows an illustrative validator run with 'profiles: 5 | rows: 41 | spine families referenced: 14/20' — that is NOT what the seed fixture produces (seed gives 'profiles: 4 | rows: 4 | spine families referenced: 2/20'); an exercise should use the real seed-fixture output, not the §5.4 prose numbers. The validator prints the summary line to stdout and FAIL lines + 'exit: 1' to stderr — in a terminal-sim these interleave naturally, but byte-exact capture via '>' alone would miss stderr (use '> file 2>&1' if the exercise checks file contents). The em-dash in 'FAIL: 1 orphan(s) — profile requirement maps to no spine control:' is U+2014; preserve it exactly. Validator does not detect duplicate rows or semantically wrong-but-valid mappings (e.g. CC7.2 -> PE-3 passes structurally) — exercise grading must layer semantic checks (expected family per requirement) on top of the validator port. happy-path.sh's awk validator emits a different output format ('DEFECT orphan PCI4 6.3.2') than the bun validator — do not conflate the two in the sim; the learner-facing one is the bun format. Framework numbering is Tier-B volatile (ISO 27002:2022 IDs like A.5.15/A.8.15, CSF 2.0 PR.AA-05/PR.DS-01, CIS v8 6.8/8.2) — pin exercise content to the module's stated editions.
